links.outcome: Local ambient scribe evaluation of note quality (PDQI-9), EHR time, and physician note contribution versus human scribes
links.effect: PDQI-9 similar for adults, lower for pediatrics with AI (41.36 vs 42.25, aRR -1.89 [95% CI -3.58 to -0.20]); more EHR notes time with AI (adult 4.3 vs 1.8 min).
links.quote: PDQI-9 scores were similar for adults, but AI scribes scored lower for pediatric patients (41.36 versus 42.25, adjusted risk ratio [aRR] = -1.89 [95% confidence interval (CI) -3.58 to -0.20]).

links.outcome: Blinded physician-rated quality of ambient scribe notes using PDQI-9 compared with human scribe notes
links.effect: Adult note quality similar; pediatric AI notes scored lower (41.36 vs 42.25, aRR -1.89 [95% CI -3.58 to -0.20]).
links.quote: PDQI-9 scores were similar for adults, but AI scribes scored lower for pediatric patients (41.36 versus 42.25, adjusted risk ratio [aRR] = -1.89 [95% confidence interval (CI) -3.58 to -0.20]).

links.outcome: Side-by-side local pilot comparing AI scribe with human scribe on quality and EHR time
links.effect: AI scribes associated with more EHR notes time, more physician note contribution, and similar to lower quality notes versus human scribes.
links.quote: In comparison to human scribes, AI scribes were associated with more time spent in the electronic health record notes section, more physician note contribution, and similar to lower quality notes.

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment of ambient AI scribes versus human scribes in an emergency department setting on EHR time and note quality metrics, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard variation.
